chapters.title: Guarded Thermal Bridge · 3D walkthrough
chapters.body: Actual browser recording of the concept model and synthetic experiment.

chapters.title: 1 · Look inside the motor
chapters.body: Orbit the assembly, then separate the parts to inspect the sensor module.

chapters.title: 2 · Two independent thermal controls
chapters.body: The shunt cools the sensing pad. A separate heater/cooler changes the guard around its leads.

chapters.title: 3 · Inspect the measurement electronics
chapters.body: Click the ADC, guard driver, and estimator. The wiring is a functional illustration.

chapters.title: 4 · Recover information after clipping
chapters.body: The direct channel stays at 95°C. Cooling the pad makes its own measurement readable again.

chapters.title: Three observations fit; the fourth checks
chapters.body: The synthetic nominal case reconstructs a 130°C winding. This is a model consistency check.

chapters.title: 5 · Why the separate guard matters
chapters.body: With strong wire leakage, changing the guard supplies information that shunt changes alone cannot.

chapters.title: 130°C recovered in the constructed example
chapters.body: A shunt-only model that ignores the wire path reports 85°C; the guarded fit recovers 130°C.

chapters.title: 6 · Test the blind spot too
chapters.body: An extra heat path bypassing the guard can defeat the fit and its fourth-state check.

chapters.title: A pass can still be wrong
chapters.body: The bypass case reports 85°C for a 130°C source. Consistency does not establish safe motor operation.
